senses.gloss:
gāthā
(‘song’)
------------------------------------------
The word, as used in the Ṛgveda, usually meant a song or a verse. In later Vedic literature including the Ṛgveda (10.85.6) and the Atharvaveda (20.127.1 to 3) as also the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa (30.32) it seems to have acquired a more technical flavour, indicating a religious, poetical, composition, but not considered as a मन्त्र, like the ṛk or the सामन्.
Two well-known gāthās need special mention here: the gāthā-nārāśaṁsī and the gāthā-raibhī. The three ṛks of the Atharvaveda mentioned above, are the first. The latter गाथा is the group of three ṛks in the same section of the Atharvaveda (20.127.4 to 6).
The nārāśaṁsī-gāthā is in praise of the deity that grants the power of speech to children.
The raibhī-gāthā enabled the ṛṣis and the performers of sacrifice to go to हेअवेन्.
